en.title: Cumulative Reward in a Coin Game
en.description:
The table starts empty. Process the events in order: i puts one coin on the table; d takes one coin away, doing nothing if the table is empty; w wins all coins on the table and clears it. Find the total number of coins won over all w events. Coins left on the table at the end do not count as rewards.

This problem uses the standard input/output format compiled by CSWork; the algorithmic rules correspond to the source problem, and the examples and test data are written by CSWork.
en.input: A single line containing the event string, of length 1 to 200, consisting only of i, d, w.
en.explanation: In example 1, consecutive d events never make the number of coins on the table negative; the last two i events put down two coins, and w wins 2 coins.
hints: Use table to track the number of coins on the table, and answer to track the number already won. On d, keep table non-negative; on w, settle first, then reset table to zero.
